title: Opaque and Fallback-Aware Pin Resolution for Model References
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a deterministic, auditable pin resolution service for model references that supports tags, semver ranges, and opaque commit hashes, with clear fallback rules and client-facing error semantics. This ticket defines the rules, API contract changes, SDK behavior, rollout strategy, and audit requirements needed to ensure predictable behavior when customers pin models by name, tag, semver range, or commit reference.
motivation: Customers pin models in different ways today (tags, semantic versions, commit hashes) and experience nondeterministic runtime behavior when a requested selector is ambiguous or when pinned variants are unavailable. We need a single server-side resolution contract that is transparent to SDKs, supports safe fallbacks, and produces audit logs for compliance and incident debugging.
proposal_summary: Define a three-tier resolution precedence: 1) exact commit hash (full or prefix), 2) exact tag name, 3) semver exact/compatible range. Introduce explicit resolution responses that include resolved_ref and resolution_path metadata (exposed in API responses and console). Provide optional client flags: 'strict_pin' (fail if not exact match), 'allow_fallbacks' (enable automatic compatible substitution), and 'fallback_policy' (prefer older stable vs newer minor). Establish error codes for ambiguous selectors and for fallback-exhausted scenarios. Add server-side validation hooks to reject incompatible profile matches with a clear migration path via warnings before enforcement.
api_contract_changes: Add 'resolved_ref' and 'resolution_reason' fields to generation and model-info endpoints
Introduce query params: strict_pin (boolean string), allow_fallbacks (boolean string), fallback_policy (string enum: prefer_stable|prefer_latest)
Return 409 with error_code 'pin_ambiguous' for ambiguous selector resolution when strict_pin=true
Return 424 with error_code 'fallback_exhausted' when no compatible variants are available and allow_fallbacks=false
sdk_behavior: SDKs should surface 'resolved_ref' and 'resolution_reason' on response objects for telemetry
Default SDK behavior: allow_fallbacks=true, fallback_policy='prefer_stable' to preserve predictable latency/cost
Expose high-level helpers: pinByHash(hash), pinByTag(tag), pinBySemver(range) that set strict_pin appropriately
Add opt-in logging hook: onPinResolution(resolution_metadata) for applications to capture audit context in their logs
failure_modes_and_errors: Ambiguous selector when multiple tags or semver matches map to different hashes -> error_code 'pin_ambiguous'
Network/registry inconsistency where commit hash exists but binary artifact missing -> error_code 'artifact_not_found' and automatic soft-fallback if allow_fallbacks=true
Resolution race: concurrent tag update causes a different resolved_ref than indicated in console -> resolution_reason includes 'race_detected' and recommended client retry with strict_pin
Semver range with no matching published versions -> error_code 'no_semver_match'
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement server resolution and opt-in SDK flags. Enable in 'dev' region for internal teams only.
Phase 2 (beta): expose resolved_ref in API responses for all customers, SDKs default to allow_fallbacks=true but emit warnings for semver pins without an exact match
Phase 3 (enforceable): add account-level policy toggle to require strict_pin for compliance-sensitive customers. Default remains backward-compatible for existing workloads.
Phase 4: deprecate undocumented implicit fallback semantics and publish migration guide
test_plan: Unit tests for resolver precedence, including edge cases like overlapping semver tags
Integration tests simulating registry mutations (tag move, new release) and verifying resolution_reason and telemetry
Chaos tests that simulate artifact unavailability during resolution and assert fallback behavior
Compatibility tests against previous SDK versions to ensure graceful handling of unknown response fields
monitoring_and_audit: Emit a 'pin_resolution' event to the observability pipeline with fields: requested_selector, resolved_ref, resolution_reason, requester_token_hash
Add console dashboard for pin_resolution frequency, ambiguous selector rate, and fallback usage over time
Persist resolution decisions in audit logs for 90 days by default, configurable per-customer
Alert when fallback rate for an account exceeds threshold (default 1% of requests)
migration_notes: Notify customers who use tag/semver pins with warnings in Console and API responses for 30 days prior to any strict enforcement
Provide a migration tool to scan usage traces and surface endpoints that would be impacted by strict_pin enforcement
Offer suggested 'pinByHash' CLI helper to capture the exact hash used during a successful run and recommend lockfile creation
open_questions: Should we permit semantic precedence overrides at org-level (e.g., prefer_latest across account)?
What retention policy is required for audited resolution events for regulated customers beyond the default 90 days?
How should partial commit-hash prefixes be validated to avoid accidental collisions at scale?
tasks: Design and document resolution precedence matrix
Implement server-side resolver and add resolved_ref to API schema
Update Go and Python SDKs to surface resolution metadata and flags
Create integration tests and canary deployment plan
Instrument observability pipeline and Console dashboard
acceptance_criteria: Server resolves selectors deterministically according to precedence in 100% of unit/integration tests
API responses include resolved_ref and resolution_reason without breaking older clients (unknown fields tolerated)
SDKs provide helpers and default to allow_fallbacks=true with a simple opt-out path
Audit events for pin_resolution are emitted and visible on Console dashboard for canary org
Migration warnings are sent to customers with semver/tag pins at least 30 days before any enforced behavior change
